main.title: Stanford CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
main.why: Detection and segmentation, video, self-supervised learning, generative models, 3D and vision-language. In English.

main.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Transformers for Image Recognition at Scale
main.why: ViT drops convolutions and runs a plain Transformer on image patches, which rivals CNNs when pretrained on enough data.

main.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
main.why: Labeled datasets limit what vision models learn, so CLIP trains on web image-caption pairs and classifies zero-shot from text prompts.

further.title: SigLIP 2: Multilingual Vision-Language Encoders with Improved Semantic Understanding, Localization, and Dense Features

main.title: DINOv3
main.why: Labels limit how far vision encoders scale, so DINOv3 trains self-supervised and uses Gram anchoring to keep dense features clean.

main.title: Faster R-CNN: Towards Real-Time Object Detection with Region Proposal Networks
main.why: Region proposals were the bottleneck of detection, so Faster R-CNN adds a region proposal network that shares the detector's features.

main.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
main.why: Two-stage detectors were too slow for real time, so YOLO predicts all boxes and classes in a single pass.

main.title: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers
main.why: Detectors relied on hand-designed anchors and non-maximum suppression, so DETR predicts the set of objects directly with a Transformer.

main.title: Ultralytics YOLO26: Unified Real-Time End-to-End Vision Models
main.why: NMS adds latency to real-time detection, so YOLO26 removes it and handles detection, segmentation and pose in one pipeline.

main.title: Segment Anything
main.why: Segmentation models were trained per task, so SAM is a promptable model trained on a huge mask dataset that segments new images zero-shot.

main.title: SAM 3: Segment Anything with Concepts
main.why: SAM segments one object per prompt, so SAM 3 finds, segments and tracks every object matching a noun phrase or example image.

main.title: Visual Instruction Tuning
main.why: LLMs could not see images, so LLaVA feeds CLIP image features through a linear layer into an LLM tuned on GPT-4-written instructions.

main.title: Qwen3-VL Technical Report
main.why: For long documents and video, Qwen3-VL feeds a SigLIP 2 encoder's features through an MLP into Qwen3 LLMs with long context.

main.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
main.why: Pixel-space diffusion is expensive, so latent diffusion, the basis of Stable Diffusion, runs in an autoencoder's latent space with cross-attention for text.

main.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers
main.why: DiT shows diffusion does not need a U-Net, and its Transformer backbone keeps improving as compute grows.

main.title: Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
main.why: Stable Diffusion 3 trains with rectified flow for straighter sampling paths and uses MM-DiT, a Transformer with separate text and image weights.

main.title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models
main.why: Wan brings the diffusion transformer to video with its own video VAE, released as open models for text-to-video, image-to-video and editing.

main.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
main.why: To render a scene from new viewpoints, NeRF fits an MLP from 3D position and view direction to color and density and volume-renders it.

main.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering
main.why: NeRF renders slowly, so 3D Gaussian Splatting optimizes a set of 3D Gaussians and rasterizes them in real time.

main.title: VGGT: Visual Geometry Grounded Transformer
main.why: 3D reconstruction usually needs slow optimization, so VGGT predicts cameras, depth and point maps from many views in one forward pass.
Off-the-shelf CLIP and BLIP failed on short product queries, so embeddings tuned on the catalog now rank ads.
Transcribing menu photos by hand was costly and slow, so DoorDash uses OCR plus an LLM, with a guardrail model that sends doubtful results to people.
